newsitem.title: GERMANY: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN RECORDS SIXTH CONSECUTIVE WIN.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN RECORDS SIXTH CONSECUTIVE WIN.

text.p: Australian Michael Doohan claimed his sixth consecutive success when he won the German 500cc motorcycling grand prix on Sunday.
World champion Doohan, riding a Honda, recovered from a poor start and pulled clear of team mate Tadayuki Okada on the 12th lap to record his eighth win of the season, out of nine races.
Okada had to settle for second place while fellow Japanese Takuma Aoki, also on a Honda, came a distant third on a sunny afternoon at Nuerburgring.
The victory allowed Doohan to extend his already almost invincible lead at the top of the world championship standings.
The 32-year-old from Brisbane now has 220 points, 107 more than second-placed Nobuatsu Aoki, who came fourth on Sunday.

With six races remaining before the end of the season, the Australian, who has won the last three world championship crowns, looks set to become the third man to win four 500c titles in succession, after Mike Hailwood and Giacomo Agostini.
